**Motivation** — why organisms act and persist — intrinsic and extrinsic motivation, needs, goals and values, the internalization of regulation, and the difference between autonomous and controlled motives; the empirical counterpart of the philosophy of autonomy under `agency` (ADR-023).

| [THEORY-046](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-046.md) v2 | Expected engagement rewards lower later interest | Deci, Koestner and Ryan (1999, [LIT-557](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-557.md)): across 55 experiments, expected tangible rewards given for working on an interesting task lowered free-choice engagement after the reward stopped (d = −0.40; children −0.43, college students −0.21), and lowered self-reported interest less (−0.15). By their study-by-study account, Cameron and Pierce's rival analysis found the same for this contingency (performance-independent rewards, −0.29), while disputing nearly everything else. Their 2001 reply (LIT-562), read here, re-codes 145 studies and finds it again: rewards offered for doing an interesting task lowered free choice, −0.35 across 57 studies. Active: both sides of the dispute find this effect. | Active |
| [THEORY-047](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-047.md) v2 | Controlled internalization yields introjection | Deci and Ryan ([LIT-558](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-558.md)) and Ryan and Deci ([LIT-559](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-559.md)): supports for relatedness and competence are enough to get a value internalized, but only as an introject or a compartmentalized identification; integration also needs autonomy support. The experimental evidence is Deci et al. (1994), as reported: the same amount of internalized behaviour correlated positively with felt freedom and enjoyment under autonomy support and negatively under control. Field studies on parenting, religion and medical training agree, correlationally. This is a historical condition on autonomy of the kind [THEORY-040](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-040.md) asks about, with empirical support, but it has not been tested against matched present endorsement or applied to manipulation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-049](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-049.md) v2 | Control lowers motivation; competence info raises | Cognitive evaluation theory, as tested by Deci, Koestner and Ryan (1999, [LIT-557](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-557.md)) and summarized by Ryan and Deci ([LIT-559](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-559.md)) and Deci and Ryan ([LIT-558](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-558.md)): rewards, feedback, deadlines and choice affect intrinsic motivation through their "functional significance". Controlling events shift the perceived locus of causality outward and undermine it; informational ones affirm competence and enhance it, but only with a sense of autonomy. The meta-analytic pattern fits, and controlling versus informational positive feedback differ by d = −0.78 in four studies. Mediation by felt control is untested for rewards. Its rival, Cameron, Banko and Pierce's account (LIT-562), finds rewards tied to a score or to beating others do not undermine. Neither side has tested mediation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-052](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-052.md) v2 | Need frustration is transdiagnostic | Vansteenkiste, Ryan and Soenens (2020, [LIT-561](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-561.md)) propose that need frustration, distinct from mere lack of satisfaction, plays "a transdiagnostic role", citing a longitudinal study in which it predicted adolescents' depressive and eating symptoms and "largely accounted for their co-occurrence". Deci and Ryan ([LIT-558](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-558.md)) had located the etiology of "various forms of psychopathology" in developmental need deprivation, with need substitutes, controlled styles and rigid patterns as the route. The evidence is correlational, mostly self-report, and from the theory's authors. A partner of the inflexibility account, not a rival. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-054](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-054.md) v4 | Autonomy is graded integration, not order | Self-determination theory orders motives on a continuum from external through introjected and identified to integrated regulation and intrinsic motivation. Ryan and Deci ([LIT-559](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-559.md)) and Deci and Ryan ([LIT-558](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-558.md)) place autonomy in integration, "congruence with one's other values and needs", and report a quasi-simplex structure and an experiment in which integrated and introjected internalization behave differently. Ryan and Deci ([LIT-560](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-560.md)) align this with hierarchical accounts but grade it. It is the empirical counterpart of [THEORY-029](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-029.md)'s negative claim. It is not shown that integration can be measured apart from endorsement, and it does not escape Velleman's dilemma. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-067](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-067.md) | Self-control needs no faculty of will | Ainslie's précis ([LIT-586](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-586.md)): hyperbolic discounting makes a smaller, sooner reward temporarily preferred, so successive "interests" conflict as in a repeated prisoner's dilemma. Treating a choice as a precedent bundles the series, and summed hyperbolic curves favour the larger, later rewards; a lapse costs credibility. Will is that recursion, not an organ. Schelling ([LIT-602](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-602.md)) describes the same divided chooser from the side of tactics: we manage our later selves as we manage other people. The mathematics of bundling is sound; that willpower works this way is argued, and the précis concedes it is hard to test directly. It is a claim about how control is achieved, not about whose control is self-governance. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-070](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-070.md) | Control allocation is a cost-benefit computation | Shenhav, Botvinick & Cohen ([LIT-585](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-585.md)) unify dACC's many reported functions as one: deciding whether, where and how much control to allocate. A control signal has an identity (a task set, a threshold, an attention template) and an intensity; its expected value is its probability-weighted payoff, with future value discounted, minus an intrinsic cost rising with intensity. dACC monitors and specifies; lateral prefrontal and subcortical structures implement. The paper reviews evidence and fits nothing, so Proposed. It does not say what the cost is, how EVC is computed, or that it governs emotion regulation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-077](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-077.md) v3 | Autonomous goals get more effort and well-being | Sheldon & Elliot (1999), [LIT-589](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-589.md): a goal is self-concordant to the degree its reasons are identified or intrinsic rather than external or introjected. In two semester-long student samples, self-concordance predicted sustained effort, and effort fully carried its link to attainment (self-concordance β = .02 and .08, ns, with effort in the model). In the same two samples attainment raised well-being more when goals were self-concordant (interaction β = .11, .23), partly through accumulated daily experiences of autonomy, competence and relatedness. Everything is self-report and correlational, and the structural models fit only after revision. It is evidence for the autonomous end of SDT's continuum, not for integration as distinct from identification. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-154](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-154.md) | Reward's effect hinges on its stated contingency | Cameron, Banko and Pierce (2001, [LIT-562](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-562.md)), re-analysing 145 studies with contingencies coded by procedure. (2021), [LIT-1974](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1974.md), read in [NOTE-1510](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1510.md) from the version of record in PMC. Active as a statement of the reported paths, checked against Tables 2, 4 and 5. It does not say the frustration causes the depression: the models are traditional cross-lagged panels without random intercepts, so their lagged paths mix stable between-person differences, the reverse path was as large as the forward one at the first lag, and every variable is a self-report. | Active |
| [THEORY-1573](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1573.md) v2 | Mortality salience effect fails to replicate | Klein et al. (2022), Many Labs 4, [LIT-1796](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1796.md), read in [NOTE-1322](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1322.md) alongside Chen et al. A preregistered replication of Study 1 of Greenberg et al. (1994; d = 1.34, N = 59), with labs assigned to an author-advised or an in-house protocol. No heterogeneity across labs and no protocol effect, under each of three exclusion rules. It tests national worldview defense, not symbolic immortality or legacy motivation. | Active |
| [THEORY-1577](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1577.md) v2 | What matters depends on others surviving us | Scheffler's 2012 Tanner Lectures, [LIT-1779](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1779.md), read in [NOTE-1298](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1298.md) in place of Death and the Afterlife ([LIT-1754](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1754.md)). Argued by thought experiments: the doomsday scenario and an infertile world. The third lecture, the commentaries and the replies are not here. | Active |
| [THEORY-1578](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1578.md) v2 | Parental care gives no evidence for altruism | A critique of Unto Others, read in full in [NOTE-1282](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1282.md). Stich rejects the arguments from imperfect belief–affect correlation, from the cost of strong affect and from redundancy, and answers the argument from fragile beliefs. It leaves egoism open, not shown true. Filed from [NOTE-1282](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1282.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-1579](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1579.md) v2 | Most feel responsible to future generations | Syropoulos et al., thirteen studies and a preregistered experiment (N = 3,175), read in full from the OSF preprint of 2023 without supplements ([NOTE-1293](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1293.md)), in place of Syropoulos and Markowitz 2021; not compared with the published version. Outcomes are self-reported, measured minutes later; responsibility is not separated from caring, and nothing measures how far the self extends. | Active |
| [THEORY-1585](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1585.md) v2 | Generativity is not altruism | Kruse and Schmitt (2012), [LIT-1691](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1691.md), read in [NOTE-1261](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1261.md) in place of McAdams and de St. Aubin (1992). Generativity is read as the psychological form of an ethical joint responsibility that lasts into very old age. Its studies, 3,308 older adults in Mexico, Spain and Germany and an intervention in Belarus, Russia and Ukraine, are summarized without numbers and, for the intervention, without a control group. | Active |
| [THEORY-1591](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1591.md) v2 | Burden framing raises legacy concern | Wade-Benzoni, Sondak and Galinsky (2010), six small experiments, read in full from the published version ([NOTE-1273](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1273.md)), in place of Wade-Benzoni 2006. The authors read the results as legacy concern, "the desire to extend the self into the future" (p. 26). Two printed p-values do not match their statistics, one of them the interaction behind Hypothesis 8. | Active |
| [THEORY-1595](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1595.md) v2 | Low self-esteem doesn't drive discrimination | A qualitative review of over 40 studies, read in full in [NOTE-1278](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1278.md): 18 experiments for and 13 against the first corollary, 7 for and 28 against the second, with no effect sizes. Only two studies measured esteem for the group itself, and both support the motive. Filed from [NOTE-1278](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1278.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-1599](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1599.md) v2 | Legacy writing nudges pro-environmental intent | Wickersham et al. (2020), 988 American adults sampled evenly by age, read in full with the supplements ([NOTE-1316](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1316.md)), in place of Zaval, Markowitz and Weber 2015, whose legacy task and scale it reuses. The eight-item Legacy Motivation Scale mixes wanting to be remembered with self-regard and felt responsibility to future generations, and only its total is analysed. No condition varies whether anyone will know what one did. | Active |
| [THEORY-1600](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1600.md) v2 | Generative legacy stands apart as its own factor | Sandoval-Obando et al. (2026), [LIT-1693](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1693.md), read in [NOTE-1260](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1260.md) in place of McAdams and de St. Aubin (1992). Four items dropped for sampling adequacy, sixteen enter the analysis, fourteen appear in the final solution without comment. Three factors: Generative Inefficacy (three reverse-coded items, a possible wording factor), Generative Action (eight) and Generative Legacy (three). Exploratory in fact, one convenience sample, no invariance test. | Active |
| [THEORY-1603](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1603.md) v2 | People seek positive identity via comparison | A textbook chapter with no new evidence, read in full in [NOTE-1315](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1315.md). It states the needs a positive social identity serves in the individual's terms (certainty, self-esteem, meaning) and reports, without a source, that where identification's components are separated, commitment predicts behaviour better than self-categorization. Filed from [NOTE-1315](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1315.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-1608](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1608.md) v2 | In-group influence is private acceptance | An Annual Review by an author of the SIDE model, read in full in [NOTE-1268](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1268.md). It rereads conformity, obedience, helping, contagion and crowd findings as bounded by shared identity, and cites a meta-analysis of 20 studies in which more prototypical leaders were more influential. Results are reported, not presented. Filed from [NOTE-1268](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1268.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-1609](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1609.md) v2 | Low future-self similarity predicts impatience | Hershfield (2011), [LIT-1702](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1702.md), read in [NOTE-1259](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1259.md) from the accepted manuscript. Following Parfit, future self-continuity has three proposed components, similarity, vividness and positivity, each measured or manipulated in studies of saving and discounting. Apart from one r = .47, the review gives no effect sizes. It suggests, untested, that late in life the future self may continue in one's offspring. | Active |
| [THEORY-1615](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1615.md) v2 | Death reminders raise in-group entitativity | One experiment, read in full in [NOTE-1297](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1297.md). The bias came entirely from rating Italians higher; identification and entitativity mediated it through their shared variance, with marginal Sobel tests. The authors' account of a self extended beyond death is a conjecture they do not test. Filed from [NOTE-1297](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1297.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-1616](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1616.md) v2 | Payoff to future generations cut cooperation | Hurlstone et al., 30 groups of six, read in full from the publisher's PDF without the supplementary materials ([NOTE-1279](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1279.md)), in place of Wade-Benzoni et al. 2012. The messages restored a fair-share norm rather than extra giving. The authors call the legacy motive "a mechanism for leveraging short-term self-interest for the long-term best interests of the collective" (p. 9); nothing in the study measures motive. | Active |
| [THEORY-1629](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1629.md) v2 | Mortality-salience effects shrink under correction | Chen, Benjamin, Guo, Lai and Heine (2025), [LIT-1730](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1730.md), read in [NOTE-1271](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1271.md) in place of Burke, Martens and Faucher (2010). 635 effects give g = 0.81 uncorrected (about r = .37); selection models and WAAP-WLS give about r = .18; PET-PEESE finds no positive effect; p-curve finds evidential value at 25% average power; z-curve's expected discovery rate is 8%. Five of nine preregistered replications succeeded. Not preregistered; its figures for Many Labs 4 do not match the version the record read. | Active |
| [THEORY-1631](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1631.md) | Lived immortality modes predict their consolation | Sturesteps (1992), [LIT-1689](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1689.md), an ANU master's thesis skimmed in [NOTE-1312](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1312.md) in place of Lifton (1979, [LIT-1714](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1714.md)). It tests Rank's three modes and Lifton's two added ones with vignettes rated as consolation, separating having a mode (availability) from accepting it. Cross-sectional; Rank's sex-difference and neuroticism hypotheses failed. The copy limits copying, so almost nothing is quoted. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1963](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1963.md) | Marshmallow waits track the reward's reliability | Kidd, Palmeri & Aslin (2013), [LIT-2730](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2730.md), read in full in [NOTE-2036](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2036.md): an experiment with 28 children, 14 per arm. It is the study [CASE-281](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-281.md) reports, and [CLAIM-744](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-744.md), which rests on that case, needs it for its first half; the record's note proposes it as a ground of that claim. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1980](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1980.md) | Marshmallow wait weakly predicts later achievement | Watts, Duncan & Quan (2018), [LIT-2752](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2752.md), read from the authors' manuscript in [NOTE-2041](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2041.md): an observational analysis of the NICHD SECCYD cohort. It confirms what [CASE-281](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-281.md) says it cannot show, that waiting predicts later life; it does not test the reliability reading. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1983](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1983.md) | Distraction from rewards lengthens delay | Mischel, Ebbesen & Zeiss (1972), [LIT-2734](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2734.md), read in [NOTE-2073](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2073.md): three experiments with nursery-school children in which the experimenters supplied the distraction. It is the attentional finding [CASE-281](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-281.md) relays from A, with the correction that the situation's organization was supplied by the experimenter. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1989](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1989.md) | Marshmallow test doesn't predict age-26 outcomes | Sperber, Vandell, Duncan & Watts (2024), [LIT-2723](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2723.md), read in full in [NOTE-2074](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2074.md): the SECCYD cohort at age 26, n = 702. It confirms, to adulthood, what [CASE-281](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-281.md) says it cannot show. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2131](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2131.md) | Hazard uncertainty yields hyperbolic discounting | Hyperbolic discounting as an average of exponentials over uncertain hazard rates, read through Fedus and colleagues because Sozou could not be fetched. Proposed until Sozou is read. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2207](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2207.md) | Flow is higher at work, happiness at leisure | Rheinberg et al. (2007), [LIT-3071](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3071.md), read in [NOTE-2297](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2297.md). One of the record's two read in-episode studies of flow and affect, both found by [LEAD-054](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-054.md). Flow and happiness/satisfaction rated at each signal correlate r = .36 raw, .30 within-person, so some of flow's positivity is reported during the episode; it corroborates [CLAIM-441](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-441.md)'s premise that flow is reported as positive, against its third exit, weakly, since the correlation is pooled and flow is a continuous score. The sharp edge is the dissociation: goal-directedness lifts flow and not happiness. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2208](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2208.md) | Flow doesn't predict later valence | Engeser and Baumann (2014), [LIT-3070](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3070.md), read in [NOTE-2298](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2298.md). The more direct of the record's two read in-episode studies of flow and affect, both found by [LEAD-054](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-054.md). Within persons flow correlates .31 with valence and .59 with positive activation at the same signal, and does not raise valence at the next. It corroborates [CLAIM-441](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-441.md)'s premise that flow is positive during the episode, against the third exit that the positivity comes after it. The sharp edges: a continuous flow score with no enjoyment item, a two-hour lag, and a sample it appears to share with Rheinberg et al. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2213](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2213.md) | Negative impact frustrates without ill-being | Martela and Ryan, read in [NOTE-2303](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2303.md) (Read). Three preregistered MTurk experiments randomise a small gain or loss to the Red Cross within a key-pressing task. The loss is noticed, raising beneficence frustration (meta-analytic d = 0.84), but negative affect, anxiety and depression do not rise; the gain raises well-being. Registered as a stand-in, in part, for [LIT-1980](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1980.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2214](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2214.md) | Beneficence is an enhancer, not a need | Martela and Ryan, read in [NOTE-2304](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2304.md) (Read). Across three MTurk studies a new four-item beneficence-frustration scale correlates with every ill-being indicator but, entered after the three established frustration scales, adds no unique variance, and the three needs fully mediate it. The authors tentatively propose the category of basic wellness enhancer and call any conclusion about beneficence premature. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2223](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2223.md) | SDT continuum holds; integrated rung unmeasured | Howard, Gagné and Bureau, read in [NOTE-2313](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2313.md) (Read). Pooled correlations among the motivation types from 486 samples and 13 scales form a simplex that one dimension explains (99.75%), with unexplained heterogeneity near 99%. Integrated regulation correlates .913 with identified regulation, with overlapping intervals; the authors call it "practically indistinguishable" and ask for the theory or the measures to change. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2236](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2236.md) | Expecting repeat choices weakens self-control | Khan and Dhar (2007), [LIT-3113](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3113.md), read in [NOTE-2326](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2326.md) for [LEAD-078](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-078.md). A recurring choice is a licence unless it is seen as a precedent: the vice share rises from 46.6-57.5% in isolation to 70-90% when the same choice is announced for next week, and falls to 53% when the chooser is told this choice is the best indicator of the next. It bears on [THEORY-067](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-067.md)'s first promotion condition, in part, and on [QUESTION-034](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-034.md)'s bargaining route. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2237](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2237.md) | Choosing in a series raises patience | Schuhr (2015), [LIT-3114](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3114.md), read in part in [NOTE-2327](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2327.md) for [LEAD-078](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-078.md). In eight one-session treatments of about thirty students each, a free series of decisions raised the mixture probability of exponential discounting by 0.307 (p = 0.019), forcing the decisions together lowered it by 0.330, and stake size did not explain it. Evidence for bundling in humans without an imposed bundle; not for bundling by self-prediction, since every decision in the series is made at once. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2241](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2241.md) | Brief mindfulness speeds responses briefly | Ge et al. (2024), [LIT-916](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-916.md), read in [NOTE-2331](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2331.md) for [LEAD-078](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-078.md). In 70 students low in trait mindfulness, monitor-and-acceptance training sped conflict and inhibition responses at post-test, left accuracy and delay discounting unchanged, and had no effect at follow-up. A dissociation of speed from discounting, not a test of whether discounting mediates a change in self-control: [ARG-206](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-206.md) holds that it does not show [CLAIM-156](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-156.md)'s route. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2282](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2282.md) | Small incentives doubled immunisation over camps | Seva Mandir ran monthly camps on fixed days in 30 villages, the same camps with 1 kg of lentils per immunisation and plates on completion in 30, and nothing new in 74. Full immunisation: 18 %, 39 % and 6 %. At least one injection did not differ between the camp arms (78 % and 74 %), so the incentive acted on completion. Cost per fully immunised child: $55.83 without incentives, $27.94 with, because the camp's fixed day served 13.4 immunisations instead of 4.5. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2296](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2296.md) | Teacher performance pay raises test scores | In AP RESt, five cells of 100 randomly assigned schools: control, group bonus, individual bonus, extra contract teacher, block grant. The bonus slope was set so that expected payouts matched the input arms' spending; in the event the inputs and the individual bonus cost Rs 10,000 per school a year and the group bonus about Rs 6,000. Two-year effects: 0.27, 0.16 and, for the pooled inputs, 0.09 SD. No difference in teacher attendance or observed classroom processes; teachers' self-reports show more homework, extra classes and practice tests. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2329](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2329.md) | Regions of the life space carry valences that direct locomotion | Lewin (1936), McGraw-Hill. The account the record expects to draw from the work, attributed under the owner's direction of 2026-11-26 that even deferred works carry the theories expected of them. It is stated from the assistant's prior knowledge, unverified until read, and grounds nothing until then. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
